commands.summary: Plan: create real geometry with geometry operations: {action: solid|mass|boolean|void|reshape|convert|freeform|edit_point|thicken|trim|rebuild|panelize|surface_shell|gridshell|member|plate, ...} or {op: pattern, ...}. Forms are extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, swept_blend of profiles (rect, circle, ring, polygon, I, H, tube...). A freeform NURBS surface or shell (roof, canopy, facade) is {action: freeform, level, surface: {by: loft, curves: [{pts: [P3...], fit: through|control|polyline, degree}]} | {by: ruled, a, b} | {by: revolve, profile, axis_a, axis_b, angle} | {by: points, rows: [[P3...]...]} | {by: network, u_curves, v_curves, degree, tolerance} (every u-curve crosses every v-curve) | {by: dome, center, radius, rise} | {by: vault, a, b, span, rise}, thickness, side: normal|reverse|center, trim: {outer, holes} in 0..1 uv}; edit_point moves control point i, j; thicken sets the shell; trim cuts it; rebuild {target, count_u, count_v, degree_u, degree_v} gives a new control net and reports the deviation. A curtain system on a freeform surface is {action: panelize, host, columns, rows, pattern: quad|triangle|diamond, planarize: rounds, mullion: {width, depth}, glass, flat, cold}; columns and rows are {by: count, n} | {by: equal, n} (equal length) | {by: width, width}, rows also {by: heights, heights: [...]} (floor lines); the receipt reports flat, cold-bent and hot-bent panels. A roof or slab on a freeform surface is {action: surface_shell, host, kind: roof|slab, layers: [{thickness, material, name}], side: normal|reverse|center, openings: [[P2...]] (plan polygons cut through)}; it follows later host edits. A diagrid, gridshell or cable net is {action: gridshell, level, host: {shape: dome, center, radius, rise, oculus} | {shape: vault, a, b, span, rise} | {shape: hypar, center, lx, ly, rise, angle} | {shape: plane, corner, w, h, angle} | {shape: paraboloid, vertex, radius, depth, hub, tilt, azimuth} (dish, antenna reflector; stands on its hub ring), kind: diagrid|gridshell|cable_net, pattern: diagrid|triangular|quad_braced|quad, count_u, count_v, supports: base|edges|corners, member: "CHS 88.9x5" (catalogue section), edge, node (ball diameter)}. A real beam or brace row is {action: member, level, start, end, section: "CHS 88.9x5", role: beam|brace, rotation}; a plate is {action: plate, level, outline: [P3...], thickness, openings: [[P3...]], material}: flat ones become slabs with holes, upright rectangular ones walls with a void opening per opening. Write lengths as bare numbers in metres and points as [x, y, z] (shortest); an angle is {v, unit}. Repeat a part with {op: pattern} instead of writing it again. A boolean works on masses and keeps both operands (`keep_tool` true): it adds a linked result mass, so make the operand with action mass, not solid. Later operations of the call name the solid, mass, freeform, panelize, surface_shell, gridshell, member or plate op i of `ops` as {by: new, slot: i}. Draft only: nothing reaches the model before Apply.

commands.summary: Plan: build geometry with a deterministic script, for many parts (frames, domes, stairs, patterns). Syntax: `local x = 1`, `for i = 1, n do ... end`, `if a then ... end`, `function f(a) return a end`, tables {1, 2} and {k = v}, `--` comments, math.*. No files, network, clock or random. Units in the script are metres and radians; write lengths as len("1200 mm") or mm(1200), angles as deg(30). Stdlib: param(name, default, {min, max}) (bounds of a value with a unit carry a unit too: min = "2 m") declares an input the person can change later (default "12 m" is a length); vec3(x, y, z) with + - * and :dot :cross :length :unit; translate(v), rot_x/rot_y/rot_z(a), rot(axis, a), m1 * m2, m * v, m * form; profile.rect(w, h), circle(r), ring(ro, ri), chs(d, t), rhs(w, h, t), shs(b, t), i, h, c, t, l(h, b, t), polygon({{x, y}, ...}), named("IPE 200") from the catalog, list(); forms: extrude(prof, a, b) a member from point a to b, sweep(path, prof) with polyline({p, ...}, closed) or arc(centre, r, a0, a1) in plan, revolve(prof, centre, r, angle), loft({{profile = p, at = v}, ...}), transform(form, m); pattern(form, n, m), pattern_linear(form, n, step), pattern_radial(form, n, total_angle, centre) give lists of forms; part(name, form, material) and parts(name, forms, material) make elements; group(name, function or list) and define_component(name, forms) + place(comp, at, rot, role) give parts stable keys group/name (a role such as "blade" or "gondola" also makes the placed group a component of that name, which counts and schedules read); boolean(cut|union|intersect, part, form) turns an extruded part without a material into a mass and adds the tool and the linked result as masses, a rerun cannot change such a part; constrain(coincident|distance|parallel|perpendicular, a, b, value) is checked at once to 1 mm; measure(a, b) or measure(x) reports a length; assert(cond, message). Blocks build whole structures from one options table with shared nodes: tower, space_frame, arch, vault, helix_stair, helix_ramp, fins, bridge, stadium_roof, surface_grid over surf.*, hypar_umbrella, membrane, perforated_panel; end with audit{strict = true} (missed nodes, clashes, floating parts); script_recipes lists their options and worked examples. A script longer than one reply allows (a call cut off as invalid JSON) goes in parts: run_script with more=true for each part but the last. Limits: 2 s CPU, 256 MB, 200000 steps and 20000 elements unless allow_many. Errors come back with line, column and a hint. Apply stores the script as a recipe; rerun_recipe changes its params later. Draft only: nothing reaches the model before Apply.

commands.summary: Plan: a whole building from a brief. Fill the typed spec; deterministic code builds levels, grid, typed walls, slabs, core, doors, windows by daylight, numbered rooms, roof, fire rating and finishes as one item. Never place the geometry yourself. Typologies: house; apartment_section (apartments of rooms); office; school. Templates on them: hotel (guest rooms, reception, restaurant), clinic (consulting rooms, wards), warehouse (storage halls, office corner), mixed_use (shops below, offices above), school_campus (canteen, sports hall), residential (apartment section). A template is an approximation: say "approximated as ..." with the reply's note. design examples: {"massing": "u", "facade": "curtain", "balconies": "balcony", "terrace": true}; {"massing": "tower_podium", "upper_from": 2, "setback": 4}; {"cantilever": 2}. Setback and cantilever step a bar or tower_podium, never l/u/courtyard wings. Data centre: tag rooms data_hall, ups_room, battery_room, cooling_plant (or name them so) and size each data hall at about dc.hall_m2_rack (3) m2 per rack; help data_center gives the fit-out. Put the brief's features in features. Room areas are built within 2 % of the asked: for a minimum, ask a little more. A total area is not a field: compare brief_check.gross_floor_area_m2 and resize rooms or the footprint. Replies with counts, metrics, gates, brief_check (with a repair patch for revise_project) and why (the rule id and value behind each decision); refused with every spec problem listed. A schematic starting point, not a checked design.

commands.summary: Plan: change a project by a merge patch on its spec (e.g. {"floors": 12}). A drafted project is rebuilt in place; an applied one (its spec is stored in the model) gets a new item that changes, adds and deletes only what differs, keeping element ids. To add a room to one floor and keep the others, send changes.storey_rooms {"<floor from 0>": [rooms]}: only that floor is re-planned, the other floors keep their elements. Elements edited by hand are kept and listed as skipped.

commands.summary: Plan: a block of buildings, one on each plot, from shared site rules: set-backs to streets (block.street_setback) and to neighbours (block.side_setback), clear spacing (block.spacing), sun spacing as a share of the taller height (block.sun_ratio), reach from a street (block.fire_access), storeys from the floor-area target (block.far_target, block.storeys_min, block.storeys_max) and the program by street exposure (block.corner_program, block.street_program). Plots and streets are rings [[x, y], ...] in metres in one frame; streets are areas. overrides is a spec merge patch for one plot (typology, floors, design); spec is the shared brief without footprint or origin; rules sets shared rules. Plots need not touch: a plot nearer than the clear distance pushes the facing edges back. Storeys set in overrides are kept; a plot they leave too narrow is refused with the rule. Give the streets around the block; an inner building reached across a yard needs a larger block.fire_access. Every plot is built in parallel by the same builder and gates as generate_project and becomes its own project (P1, P2...) and plan item; Apply writes the block in one step. Use one call for all the buildings of a site, not one generate_project each. Refused with every plot's reason when one does not build or the block breaks a rule; nothing is drafted then. revise_project changes one building afterwards.

Pins by kind: distance, clear, slope two; angle two lines or three points (vertex second); area, perimeter one face or three or more points; volume one element. A pin is a point [x, y, z] in metres or a feature that follows its element: level:ID, room:ID, wall:ID@face0|face1|axis|top|bottom, floor:ID@top|bottom, mass:ID@top|bottom|north|south|east|west or @<face tag>, or wall:ID, floor:ID, mass:ID alone (its bounding box, which carries the volume). commands.summary: Plan: route a whole network from a source to target connectors. The router keeps clear of structure and other runs, cuts sleeves and slab holes, gives drains their fall, sizes every piece by flow and adds the fittings. Replies with the metrics of three variants. State the intent: never hand-place points. Air ducts: friction_pa_m sizes by equal friction and the metrics carry the critical path loss.

Circuits of a panel: devices, load, current, breaker, cable, length, voltage drop and findings, with totals and a table in English or Russian.
Definition text of a project family, to edit it as a draft.
The family definition text reference: statements, units, the findings codes. Read it once before the first family_draft.

text.description: The family definition text, one statement per line (not a path, not a URL)

base_family.description: A project family this draft edits

name.description: Draft name; default: the family name in the text

commands.summary: Offer a family definition as a draft in the family editor. The text is checked first; an invalid text is refused with the report. Nothing reaches the project until the person loads the draft.

required.description: yes or no; blank means yes

rule.description: non_empty, one_of, range, regex or unit

unit.description: Unit of the range or the unit rule: mm, m, m2

value.description: Values `a; b`, range `0.9..2.4`, or a pattern

text.description: What the person asked for, in their words

commands.summary: Read information requirements from a workbook path or from rows and offer them to the person, who saves them as the project's requirements. Every refused cell is listed with sheet, row and column; nothing is saved while any is refused.

atomic.description: true: any failed write takes the whole group out of the draft again. Default false: a failed write is reported and leaves nothing, the earlier writes stay and the group stays open

title.description: Shown to the person in the audit log

commands.summary: Start a group of writes in your draft. Pass the returned handle to each following call. A failed write answers op_failed with its own error and leaves nothing; earlier writes stay. Pass atomic: true to take the whole group out on any failure.
Close the group: its writes stay queued in your draft until the person presses Apply. Answers queued with the draft number and pending_user.
Drop the group from your draft: nothing reaches the model.

Your draft of this connection: number, pending operations with element counts, stale when the model changed since, and whether the person applied or discarded it. Writes never reach the model before the person's Apply.
Reject your draft: drop every pending operation. Nothing reaches the model.

Ask the person to apply your draft: the editor puts its card before them and answers awaiting_user, naming any check that blocks Apply. Only the person's Apply writes the model; follow with draft_status (last.state applied or discarded).
State of the batches waiting for the person: waiting, applied, rejected or stale.

commands.summary: Dry-run an ops envelope and leave it on a plan card for the person. It is applied only when the person presses Apply; this tool never writes. Follow it with plan_status.
Project file name, units, levels with element counts, and model totals.

commands.summary: Write the project as an IFC file into the project's exports folder (next to the saved project). Only a plain file name is accepted; the model does not change.
